clause: 12. WAIVER OF RIGHTS. Tenant waives all rights and remedies afforded under Chapter 59.18 RCW and agrees that no provision of that chapter shall apply to this tenancy.
why: A blanket waiver of the chapter is void under (2)(a).

clause: 12. GOVERNING LAW. This Agreement is governed by Washington law, and nothing in it limits any right or remedy Tenant has under Chapter 59.18 RCW.
why: Affirms the chapter rather than waiving it.

clause: 12. SEVERABILITY. If any provision of this Agreement is later found to waive a right under Chapter 59.18 RCW, that provision alone is unenforceable and the remainder of this Agreement stays in effect.
why: Names waiver and the chapter, but disclaims the waiver instead of imposing one.

clause: 18. CLAIMS AGAINST LANDLORD. Tenant waives any right to bring, join, or otherwise participate in any class action against Landlord or Landlord's agents.
why: Waiving class participation is prohibited by (2)(b).

clause: 18. CLAIMS AGAINST LANDLORD. Tenant may bring or join any action against Landlord individually or as a member of a class, to the full extent permitted by law.
why: Preserves the right (2)(b) protects.

clause: 18. CLAIMS AGAINST LANDLORD. Landlord shall not treat Tenant's participation in a class action, or in any other proceeding against Landlord, as a breach of this Agreement or as grounds for nonrenewal.
why: Discusses class actions at length while protecting rather than restricting them.

clause: 9. CONFIDENTIALITY. Tenant shall not disclose the rent amount, any concession, move-in gift, or lease special under this Agreement to any current or prospective tenant of the property.
why: A nondisclosure agreement covering rent terms is prohibited by (2)(c).

clause: 9. DISCLOSURE. Tenant may discuss the rent amount, any concession, and any other term of this Agreement with anyone, including other tenants of the property.
why: Explicitly permits what (2)(c) protects.

clause: 9. CONFIDENTIALITY OF APPLICATION MATERIALS. Landlord shall keep Tenant's rental application, credit report, and income documentation confidential and shall not release them to third parties without Tenant's written consent. Nothing in this section restricts Tenant from discussing rent, deposits, or any lease term with any person.
why: Carries a CONFIDENTIALITY heading and a real nondisclosure obligation — on the landlord, not the tenant.

clause: 22. CONFESSION OF JUDGMENT. Tenant authorizes Landlord's attorney to appear on Tenant's behalf and confess judgment against Tenant on any claim arising out of this Agreement.
why: Authorizing a confession of judgment is prohibited by (2)(d).

clause: 22. DISPUTES. Any claim arising out of this Agreement shall be decided by a court of competent jurisdiction in the county where the premises are located, with each party appearing on its own behalf.
why: Routes disputes to a court instead of a confessed judgment.

clause: 22. CONFESSION OF JUDGMENT. No person is authorized to confess judgment against Tenant on any claim arising out of this Agreement, and any such authorization elsewhere in this Agreement is void.
why: Same heading and vocabulary as the prohibited version, opposite effect.

clause: 5. ATTORNEYS' FEES. In any action or dispute arising out of this Agreement, Tenant agrees to pay all of Landlord's attorneys' fees and costs, regardless of the outcome of the action.
why: Tenant paying the landlord's fees outside a court award is prohibited by (2)(e).

clause: 5. ATTORNEYS' FEES. In any action arising out of this Agreement, the prevailing party may recover reasonable attorneys' fees and costs as awarded by the court.
why: Prevailing-party fees awarded by a court are the exception (2)(e) allows.

clause: 5. COSTS AND FEES. Each party shall bear its own attorneys' fees and costs, except where a court awards fees to a party under Chapter 59.18 RCW or other applicable law.
why: Names attorneys' fees, the landlord-tenant chapter, and an exception — the shape of the clause the judge has to read carefully.

clause: 14. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. Landlord shall not be liable for any injury to persons or loss of property occurring on the premises from any cause whatsoever, and Tenant shall indemnify and hold Landlord harmless from any such claim.
why: Exculpation plus indemnity is prohibited by (2)(f).

clause: 14. LIABILITY. Each party is responsible for loss or injury caused by its own negligence. Nothing in this Agreement limits any liability Landlord has arising under law.
why: Declines the exculpation (2)(f) prohibits.

clause: 14. RENTER'S INSURANCE. Tenant is encouraged, but not required, to carry renter's insurance covering Tenant's personal property, since Landlord's policy does not insure Tenant's belongings. This section does not limit or shift any liability Landlord has arising under law.
why: Talks about landlord coverage not extending to tenant property, which reads adjacent to exculpation.

clause: 27. ARBITRATION. The parties agree that all disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be heard by Cascade Arbitration Services, the arbitrator selected by the parties as of the date of this Agreement.
why: Agreeing to a particular arbitrator at signing is prohibited by (2)(g).

clause: 27. ARBITRATION. If both parties later agree to arbitrate a dispute, they shall select the arbitrator by mutual agreement at the time the dispute arises.
why: Arbitrator chosen after the dispute, not at signing.

clause: 27. MEDIATION AND ARBITRATION. Either party may propose a mediator or arbitrator after a dispute arises. Neither party is bound to any mediator or arbitrator named in advance of a dispute, and no such person is designated by this Agreement.
why: Names arbitrators repeatedly while refusing to designate one.

clause: 28. ARBITRATION COSTS. Tenant agrees to arbitrate all disputes arising out of this Agreement and to share the cost of the arbitration equally with Landlord.
why: Arbitration without the landlord paying the entire cost is prohibited by (2)(h).

clause: 28. ARBITRATION COSTS. If the parties arbitrate a dispute, Landlord shall pay the entire cost of the arbitration, and this Agreement has been notarized as required.
why: Meets both conditions (2)(h) sets.

clause: 28. ARBITRATION. Arbitration of a dispute under this Agreement is available only where Landlord pays the entire cost of the arbitration and the agreement to arbitrate is notarized. Tenant is not otherwise required to arbitrate any claim.
why: Restates the statutory conditions as a limit on the landlord.

clause: 3. LATE CHARGES. If rent is not received by 11:59 PM on the first day of the month, Tenant shall pay a late charge of $75, plus $10 for each additional day the rent remains unpaid.
why: A late fee inside the five-day grace period is prohibited by (2)(i).

clause: 3. LATE CHARGES. A late charge of $50 applies only if rent remains unpaid more than five days after its due date.
why: Respects the five-day grace period.

clause: 3. LATE CHARGES. No late charge will be assessed on rent paid within five days following its due date. If rent is more than five days past due, a late charge of $50 may be charged commencing from the first day after the due date until paid.
why: Quotes the statute's own wording, including the part that permits back-dating the fee after day five.

clause: 4. RENT PAYMENT. Rent shall be paid by electronic funds transfer through Landlord's online portal only. No other method of payment will be accepted.
why: Electronic-means-only payment is prohibited by (2)(j).

clause: 4. RENT PAYMENT. Tenant may pay rent by personal check, cashier's check, money order, or electronic transfer through Landlord's online portal.
why: This is the clause the gold set caught being flagged red once the enumerated split reached the judge.

clause: 4. RENT PAYMENT. Landlord provides an online portal for electronic rent payment as a convenience to Tenant. Tenant may instead mail a check or money order to the address in Section 1, or deliver payment in person during office hours.
why: Leads with the electronic method and only then offers alternatives — the wording most likely to read as electronic-only.

clause: 2. RENT. Monthly rent is $1,600, due on the first day of each month. Rent may be paid by personal check, cashier's check, money order, or electronic transfer, at Tenant's choice.
why: Verbatim from evaluation/leases/lease_clean.md — the compliant lease. A paraphrase would not settle whether the enumerated split reproduces the gold set's false red, so the actual clause is in the set.

clause: 2. RENT. Rent is $2,450 per month, due on the first. Payments may be made by check, money order, or electronic transfer through the resident portal.
why: Verbatim from evaluation/leases/lease_04_heavy.md. Lawful on its own terms even though that lease carries planted violations elsewhere.

clause: 2. RENT. Tenant will pay $1,925 per month, due on the first day of each month, by check or electronic payment to Landlord at the address provided.
why: Verbatim from evaluation/leases_synthetic/lease_synth_012_violations.md. TWO methods, terse, no 'at Tenant's choice' — and the judge's own explanation under the enumerated split reads 'requires rent payment by check or electronic payment ONLY', a word the clause does not contain. This shape is what the first version of this set missed: its permissive (2)(j) clauses all listed three or four methods, which reads as an open menu, while a bare two-item list reads as a closed one.

clause: 2. RENT AMOUNT AND PAYMENT. The monthly rent is $2,200, due on the first day of each month. Rent should be paid by check or electronic transfer to the Landlord's designated account.
why: Verbatim from evaluation/leases_synthetic/lease_synth_029_clean.md — a COMPLIANT lease, which is the worst place to raise a red flag. Same hallucinated 'only' in the explanation.

clause: 2. RENT. Payments shall be made by check or electronic transfer as directed by the Landlord.
why: Verbatim payment sentence from lease_synth_040_injection.md. 'shall be made ... as directed by the Landlord' is the most mandatory-sounding of the three while still naming a non-electronic method.
